the magnitude of signaling responses to ECM and growth factors is attenuated with aging in human mammary epithelia.

the magnitude of signaling through the MAPK and PI3K pathways in human mammary epithelium declines with age and this decline is accompanied by increased susceptibility to oncogene-induced senescent transformation.
microenvironmental cell signalling is attenuated with aging in human mammary epithelium, which may contribute to the increased breast cancer incidence in post-menopausal women.

the study of the mechanisms of age-related changes in microenvironmental cell-signaling and their impact on breast cancer risk.
the role of the microenvironment in breast carcinogenesis and how this role changes with age.
understanding how aging affects cell signaling and lineage fidelity in human mammary epithelia, and how these changes may increase breast cancer susceptibility in post-menopausal women.
